tasks.title: session_mcp: thin stdio MCP transport shim behind __main__, import-pure
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/session_mcp.py imports cleanly with the mcp SDK ABSENT: the FastMCP import is guarded in try/except ImportError and 'mcp' not in sys.modules after importing the module.
Each tool callable delegates to the matching SessionApi method and returns its identical dict unchanged.
FastMCP construction and server .run() occur ONLY under if __name__ == '__main__': — importing the module has no side effect and runs no server.
No transport call lives inside the fuzz-gated handler path; the module is a thin transport over SessionApi only.

spec.objective: Implement ngv2/session_mcp.py: a thin stdio MCP transport that registers exactly three tools (create_session, submit_artifacts, transition) delegating straight through to SessionApi, with the FastMCP import guarded so the module imports with no side effect and only the __main__ path needs the mcp SDK.
functional_requirements: The module imports cleanly when the mcp SDK is absent by guarding the FastMCP import in try/except ImportError, and after importing the module 'mcp' is not in sys.modules.
build_tools(api) returns a dict whose keys are EXACTLY {'create_session','submit_artifacts','transition'} and whose values are callables.
Each tool callable dispatches to the matching SessionApi method (create_session/submit_artifacts/transition) and returns that method's identical dict result.
FastMCP construction and .run() are placed only under if __name__ == '__main__':; importing the module performs no server construction and no run, leaving zero import side effects.
spec.interfaces: def build_tools(api) -> dict[str, callable] with keys {'create_session','submit_artifacts','transition'}; a guarded `try: from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP / except ImportError: FastMCP = None`; and an `if __name__ == '__main__':` block that constructs FastMCP, registers the build_tools callables, and calls .run() over stdio. api is a SessionApi instance from C1.
edge_cases: Importing session_mcp with the mcp SDK not installed succeeds and leaves 'mcp' not in sys.modules (the guarded import does not pull the SDK in at import time).
build_tools(api) returns exactly the three required keys — no extra/missing tools — and each callable forwards args to the matching SessionApi method.
Calling a built tool returns the exact dict object the SessionApi method returned, with no wrapping or mutation.
spec.non_goals: No FastAPI/Flask/http.server, no bound network socket, no top-level FastMCP construction or .run(), no duplication of the legacy NobleGreed/services/mcp_server.py task/feedback tools, and no integration logic inside the transport beyond pure delegation to SessionApi. No new schema.
spec.implementation_notes:
Copy the stdio FastMCP shape from legacy NobleGreed/services/mcp_server.py (from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP) but only the shape, not its tools — this server's domain is session phase control. Guard the SDK import so the import-purity oracle passes without mcp in requirements. Keep build_tools a pure factory returning thin lambdas/closures over api methods; defer all FastMCP wiring and .run() to the __main__ guard. Differential fuzz is bypassed for this leaf (mcp_plumbing) — the import-purity + registration oracle is load-bearing.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.
spec.structure_directive: MODULE STRUCTURE (MANDATORY — the oracle asserts import-purity AND __main__-guarding): At MODULE TOP-LEVEL do NOT import mcp/FastMCP in ANY form (not even guarded try/except) — if mcp is installed even a guarded import puts 'mcp' in sys.modules and the import-purity test FAILS. The string '.run(' must appear ONLY textually AFTER the `if __name__ == "__main__":` line. Required shape: (1) module top imports only stdlib + `from ngv2.session_api import SessionApi` (and SessionDB if needed); (2) define pure tool callables and `def build_tools(api): return {'create_session': lambda session_id, target_spec: api.create_session(session_id, target_spec), 'submit_artifacts': lambda session_id, phase, artifacts: api.submit_artifacts(session_id, phase, artifacts), 'transition': lambda session_id, to_phase: api.transition(session_id, to_phase)}` — EXACTLY those three keys, each delegating to and returning the matching SessionApi method's dict; (3) put the ENTIRE server wiring INSIDE `if __name__ == "__main__":` — and ONLY there: `from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP` (deferred import), construct FastMCP, build a SessionApi over a real SessionDB, register build_tools(api) entries, and call server.run(). No `.run(` anywhere above the guard. Importing the module must have ZERO side effects and must NOT import mcp. NO time.time/datetime/random.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: A stub SessionApi recording calls and returning sentinel dicts; an import harness run with 'mcp' removed/absent from sys.modules to assert import purity; introspection of the module source to confirm .run() appears only under the __main__ guard.

token_budget_ratio.note: Transport shim is tiny; the oracle (import purity + exact tool registration + delegation) is load-bearing since differential fuzz is bypassed, so tests dominate the budget.

tasks.title: session_api: pure SessionApi handler over injected SessionDB
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/session_api.py defines SessionApi(db) as a pure class over an injected SessionDB; no transport, no network, no socket import.
create_session(session_id, target_spec) persists a session at phase 'hunt' via the existing session_pipeline table and returns {'ok':True,'session_id','phase':'hunt'}.
get_state(session_id) returns {'ok':True,'session_id','phase','target_spec'} for a known id and {'ok':False,'status':404,'error':<str>} for an unknown id.

submit_artifacts(session_id, phase, artifacts) rebuilds each to_dict() artifact and runs contract validate() BEFORE write; invalid artifacts are never persisted; returns {'ok':True,'accepted':<int>,'rejected':[{'index':<int>,'error':<str>},...]} with partial accept and input-index-carrying rejects.

transition(session_id, to_phase) delegates to session_gate.gate_transition + phase_runner.get_next_phase and writes a phase_validation_logs audit row via append_phase_validation_log on EVERY attempt (allowed+gate-pass advances and returns ok True with from/to; disallowed returns {'ok':False,'status':422,'error':<str>} with phase unchanged + failed audit row; allowed-but-gate-fails returns ok False, phase unchanged, audit row still written).

Every method is deterministic given the injected store: no time.time(), datetime.now(), or random; any timestamp is taken from an injected now_fn or omitted. Audit rows are read via get_phase_validation_logs().
No new SQLite schema is introduced; session phase is persisted/read through Epic B's existing session_pipeline table on the injected db.

spec.objective: Implement ngv2/session_api.py: a pure, deterministic SessionApi(db) handler exposing create_session, get_state, submit_artifacts, and transition over an injected Epic-B SessionDB, returning only JSON-serializable dicts and writing a phase_validation_logs audit row on every transition attempt.
functional_requirements: create_session(session_id, target_spec) writes a new session row at phase 'hunt' through the existing session_pipeline table and returns {'ok':True,'session_id':session_id,'phase':'hunt'}.
get_state(session_id) returns {'ok':True,'session_id','phase','target_spec'} for a known session and {'ok':False,'status':404,'error':<str>} for an unknown session id.

submit_artifacts(session_id, phase, artifacts) treats artifacts as a list of to_dict() forms, rebuilds and validate()-checks each (Finding/PoC/LiveTestReport) BEFORE writing, never persists an invalid artifact, supports partial accept, and returns {'ok':True,'accepted':<int>,'rejected':[{'index':<int>,'error':<str>},...]} with rejected carrying the input index.

transition(session_id, to_phase) for an allowed phase whose gate_transition passes advances the session via phase_runner.get_next_phase and returns {'ok':True,'session_id','from','to'}, writing a passing audit row.

transition(session_id, to_phase) for a disallowed phase returns {'ok':False,'status':422,'error':<str>} leaving the phase unchanged and writing a FAILED audit row; for an allowed phase whose gate fails it returns ok False with phase unchanged while still writing an audit row.

Every transition attempt (pass, gate-fail, disallowed) writes exactly one phase_validation_logs audit row via append_phase_validation_log(...), readable through get_phase_validation_logs(); all methods are deterministic over the injected store with no wall-clock or random calls.
spec.interfaces: class SessionApi: def __init__(self, db, now_fn=None); create_session(session_id, target_spec)->dict; get_state(session_id)->dict; submit_artifacts(session_id, phase, artifacts)->dict; transition(session_id, to_phase)->dict. Consumes ngv2.session_db.SessionDB, ngv2.session_gate.gate_transition/GateResult, ngv2.phase_runner.get_next_phase, and ngv2.contracts Finding/PoC/LiveTestReport.validate(). Pure: JSON-serializable dicts only, no transport, no network, no socket.
edge_cases: get_state on an unknown session_id returns {'ok':False,'status':404,'error':<str>} without raising.

submit_artifacts with a mix of one invalid Finding and one valid Finding accepts only the valid one (accepted==1), never persists the invalid one, and reports rejected with the invalid artifact's input index.
transition to a disallowed phase returns a 422-style error dict, leaves the session phase unchanged, and still writes a FAILED phase_validation_logs audit row.
transition to an allowed phase whose gate_transition fails returns ok False with phase unchanged and still writes an audit row for the attempt.
spec.non_goals: No FastAPI/Flask/http.server, no bound network socket, no new SQLite schema (reuse the existing session_pipeline table), no MCP transport calls inside this handler, and no integration with the legacy NobleGreed/services/mcp_server.py task/feedback tools. No wall-clock or random usage.
spec.implementation_notes:
Follow the cleanroom shape of JanusMaskJR overseer/web_api.py (OverseerWebApi pure class over an injected store) without importing it. Persist/read phase via the injected SessionDB's session_pipeline accessors. Build contract objects from each artifact to_dict() and call validate() before any write so invalid artifacts never reach the store. Write the audit row on every transition branch via append_phase_validation_log(...). If a timestamp is required, accept an injected now_fn (WorkerRegistry convention) rather than calling time/datetime. Do not allowlist until Epic B is green.

Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.
spec.persistence_directive: PERSISTENCE (MANDATORY — do NOT silently no-op): SessionDB has NO public session helper and its session_pipeline table is (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, phase TEXT, data TEXT). Persist session state by writing SQL DIRECTLY through the injected db's sqlite connection `self.db._conn` against the EXISTING session_pipeline table (NO new table/column). create_session: INSERT a row with phase='hunt' and data=json.dumps({'session_id':session_id,'target_spec':target_spec,'phase':'hunt'}). get_state: `SELECT data FROM session_pipeline WHERE json_extract(data,'$.session_id')=?` and return the 404 dict if no row. transition: UPDATE that row's phase and data json. Do NOT search for a non-existent insert_session/add_session helper and skip the write — there is none; emit the SQL yourself. Use json.dumps/json.loads (deterministic, sort_keys ok) — NO time.time()/datetime/random.
spec.transition_directive: CALL REAL APIs DIRECTLY — do NOT build adaptive _invoke/_find_method/pool shims that guess signatures (they caused 'gate_transition() missing rows'). Exact contracts: (1) gate_transition is `from ngv2.session_gate import gate_transition` with signature gate_transition(rows, from_phase, to_phase)->GateResult(.ok,.error); rows={'findings':[...],'pocs':[...],'reports':[...]} where each list is the JSON dicts from the db: build via direct SQL on self.db._conn — findings=[json.loads(r['data']) for r in self.db._conn.execute('SELECT data FROM findings')], pocs=[... FROM pocs], reports=[... FROM live_test_reports]. (2) ALLOWED check: `to_phase in ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.get(current_phase, ())` (import ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS from ngv2.state_machine) OR reuse phase_runner; do NOT use a (a,b) tuple key. (3) transition(session_id,to_phase) FLOW: st=self.get_state(session_id); if not st['ok'] return st(404). current=st['phase']. allowed = to_phase in ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.get(current,()). gr=gate_transition(rows,current,to_phase). ok = allowed and gr.ok. ALWAYS write an audit row BEFORE returning, on EVERY attempt (allowed, disallowed, gate-fail): self.db.append_phase_validation_log({'session_id':session_id,'from':current,'to':to_phase,'ok':ok,'error':(None if ok else (gr.error if not gr.ok else 'transition not allowed'))}, phase=to_phase). Then: if not allowed -> return {'ok':False,'status':422,'error':<str>}; elif not gr.ok -> return {'ok':False,'status':422,'error':gr.error}; else advance the session row's phase (UPDATE session_pipeline data+phase) and return {'ok':True,'session_id':session_id,'from':current,'to':to_phase}. submit_artifacts must persist accepted artifacts via the real SessionDB helpers insert_finding/insert_poc/insert_report after validate(). NO time.time/datetime/random.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: A fake/in-memory SessionDB implementing the session_pipeline phase accessors plus append_phase_validation_log/get_phase_validation_logs; valid and invalid Finding to_dict() fixtures; allowed and disallowed to_phase values against a session seeded at phase 'hunt'.

token_budget_ratio.note: Pure handler logic is compact; the load-bearing value is the oracle exercising every transition branch and the validate-before-write path, so tests dominate.
